gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the single-USB-C-cable mode on a two-screen extender is a display-driver mode: DeskGearHQ says the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro's 'single USB-C cable drives both panels' and that none of its picks need a driver, but our Trio 3 Pro record says it runs driver-free only with one video-capable USB-C port per screen, and our FOPO S788 record says it needs the UsbDisplay driver in every mode.
standout_why: Compared against DeskGearHQ (2026-07-26), which I opened. It calls the Trio 3 Pro's one-cable hookup driver-free and never mentions base-MacBook display limits. Plugable's USBC-MSTH2 page (cited) covers only its own $39.95 adapter: no driver, and on macOS one extended plus one mirrored display. ChatGPT's own answer gives the general advice to avoid DisplayLink but does not name a single extender whose one-cable mode needs a driver. I could not open the other cited pages: fopomonitor.com S11 and tutt.ca returned HTTP 429, Best Buy timed out, and gradedpicks.com failed on a certificate error. So I can't rule out that the FOPO S11 page explains its own cabling.
decides: For 'without drivers' the deciding check is one video-capable USB-C port (or HDMI) per added screen, and how many external displays the laptop drives. Apple's spec page says a MacBook Air M2 drives one external display. So on a base M-series MacBook, or a laptop with a single video port, a dual extender extends only one screen without a driver, and a one-screen native Alt Mode extender is the honest pick: the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS (ours). On Windows laptops with two video outputs, the FOPO dual extenders listed as driver-free (S1 for the lowest cost, S7 for 16:10 at 14 inches, S11 for 16 inches) win the two-screen segment. The FOPO S788 drops out because it needs a driver. The Trio 3 Pro drops out in single-cable mode and qualifies only with two cables.
